# zgesvd

> Computes the singular value decomposition (SVD) of a complex M-by-N matrix A.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zgesvd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zgesvd';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zgesvd(
    order,
    jobu, jobvt,
    M, N,
    A, LDA,
    s, strideS,
    U, LDU,
    VT, LDVT,
    WORK,
    RWORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' 0 'column-major') |
| `jobu` | `"all-columns" \| "economy" \| "overwrite" \| "none"` | `'all-columns'`: all M columns of U returned, `'economy'`: first min(M,N) columns, `'overwrite'`: overwrite A, `'none'`: no U |
| `jobvt` | `"all-rows" \| "economy" \| "overwrite" \| "none"` | `'all-rows'`: all N rows of V^H returned, `'economy'`: first min(M,N) rows, `'overwrite'`: overwrite A, `'none'`: no VT<br>Rejects `!(((jobvt === 'all-rows' \|\| jobvt === 'economy') \|\| jobvt === 'overwrite') \|\| jobvt === 'none') \|\| (jobvt === 'overwrite' && jobu === 'overwrite')` |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of A<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Column-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, M)`<br>Row-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `s` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length min(M, N)</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | `s` stride length |
| `U` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × (jobu === 'all-columns' ? M : min(M, N))</sub> | **out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDU` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `U`<br>Rejects `ldu < 1 \|\| ((jobu === 'all-columns' \|\| jobu === 'economy') && ldu < M)` |
| `VT` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDVT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VT`<br>Rejects `(ldvt < 1 \|\| (jobvt === 'all-rows' && ldvt < N)) \|\| (jobvt === 'economy' && ldvt < min(M, N))` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ MINWRK</sub> | **out** · Complex workspace of at least the reference's MINWRK (at most `max( 1, 2*min(M,N) + max(M,N) )`), or `null` to allocate the reference's MAXWRK, which enables the fast QR/LQ paths and the callees' blocked code |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * min(M, N)</sub> | **out** · Real workspace, or `null` to auto-allocate at the minimum required size (`max(1, 5*min(M,N))`) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobu`: Specifies options for computing all or part of the matrix U:

  -   `= 'A'`: all M columns of U are returned in array U:
  -   `= 'S'`: the first min(m,n) columns of U (the left singular vectors) are returned in the array U;
  -   `= 'O'`: the first min(m,n) columns of U (the left singular vectors) are overwritten on the array A;
  -   `= 'N'`: no columns of U (no left singular vectors) are computed.
- `jobvt`: Specifies options for computing all or part of the matrix $V^H$:

  -   `= 'A'`: all N rows of $V^H$ are returned in the array `VT`;
  -   `= 'S'`: the first min(m,n) rows of $V^H$ (the right singular vectors) are returned in the array `VT`;
  -   `= 'O'`: the first min(m,n) rows of $V^H$ (the right singular vectors) are overwritten on the array A;
  -   `= 'N'`: no rows of $V^H$ (no right singular vectors) are computed.

  `JOBVT` and `JOBU` cannot both be 'O'.
- `M`: The number of rows of the input matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the input matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, if `JOBU = 'O'`, A is overwritten with the first min(m,n)

  -   columns of U (the left singular vectors,
  -   stored columnwise);

  if `JOBVT = 'O'`, A is overwritten with the first min(m,n)

  -   rows of $V^H$ (the right singular vectors,
  -   stored rowwise);

  if $\mathrm{JOBU} \ne \text{'O'}$ and $\mathrm{JOBVT} \ne \text{'O'}$, the contents of A

  are destroyed.
- `s`: The singular values of A, sorted so that $S(i) \ge S(i+1)$.
- `U`: (`LDU`,M) if `JOBU = 'A'` or (`LDU`,min(M,N)) if `JOBU = 'S'`. If `JOBU = 'A'`, U contains the M-by-M unitary matrix U; if `JOBU = 'S'`, U contains the first min(m,n) columns of U (the left singular vectors, stored columnwise); if `JOBU = 'N'` or 'O', U is not referenced.
- `VT`: If `JOBVT = 'A'`, `VT` contains the N-by-N unitary matrix $V^H$; if `JOBVT = 'S'`, `VT` contains the first min(m,n) rows of $V^H$ (the right singular vectors, stored rowwise); if `JOBVT = 'N'` or 'O', `VT` is not referenced.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.
- `RWORK`: On exit, if $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, `RWORK(1:MIN(M,N)-1)` contains the unconverged superdiagonal elements of an upper bidiagonal matrix B whose diagonal is in S (not necessarily sorted). B satisfies $A = U \, B \, \mathrm{VT}$, so it has the same singular values as A, and singular vectors related by U and `VT`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all-columns", "none", "overwrite", "economy"
- `TypeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `!( ( ( jobvt === "all-rows" \|\| jobvt === "economy" ) \|\| jobvt === "overwrite" ) \|\| jobvt === "none" ) \|\| ( jobvt === "overwrite" && jobu === "overwrite" )`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDU < 1 \|\| ( ( jobu === "all-columns" \|\| jobu === "economy" ) && LDU < M )`)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDU < 1 \|\| ( ( jobu === "all-columns" \|\| jobu === "economy" ) && LDU < max( 1, jobu === "all-columns" ? M : min( M, N ) ) )`)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `( LDVT < 1 \|\| ( jobvt === "all-rows" && LDVT < N ) ) \|\| ( jobvt === "economy" && LDVT < min( M, N ) )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zgesvd.ndarray(
    jobu, jobvt,
    M, N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    s, strideS, offsetS,
    U, strideU1, strideU2, offsetU,
    VT, strideVT1, strideVT2, offsetVT,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork
) → info: integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobu` | `"all-columns" \| "economy" \| "overwrite" \| "none"` | `'all-columns'`: all M columns of U returned, `'economy'`: first min(M,N) columns, `'overwrite'`: overwrite A, `'none'`: no U |
| `jobvt` | `"all-rows" \| "economy" \| "overwrite" \| "none"` | `'all-rows'`: all N rows of V^H returned, `'economy'`: first min(M,N) rows, `'overwrite'`: overwrite A, `'none'`: no VT<br>Rejects `!(((jobvt === 'all-rows' \|\| jobvt === 'economy') \|\| jobvt === 'overwrite') \|\| jobvt === 'none') \|\| (jobvt === 'overwrite' && jobu === 'overwrite')` |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of A<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix (column-major) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A (in complex elements) |
| `s` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length min(M, N)</sub> | **out** · Output array of real singular values (length min(M,N)) |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | Stride for s |
| ↳ `offsetS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for s |
| `U` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>M × (jobu === 'all-columns' ? M : min(M, N))</sub> | **out** · Output matrix for left singular vectors |
| ↳ `strideU1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of U (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideU2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of U (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for U (in complex elements) |
| `VT` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix for right singular vectors |
| ↳ `strideVT1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of VT (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideVT2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of VT (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetVT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for VT (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ MINWRK</sub> | **out** · Complex workspace of at least the reference's MINWRK, `computeMinWorkSize( jobu, jobvt, M, N )` complex elements from `offsetWork` (`3*min(M,N)` when M is much larger than N with jobu `'none'`, or N much larger than M with jobvt `'none'`; otherwise `2*min(M,N) + max(M,N)`); the reference's MAXWRK, `computeWorkSize( jobu, jobvt, M, N )`, enables the fast QR/LQ paths and the callees' blocked code |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK (in complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * min(M, N)</sub> | **out** · Caller-owned real workspace of at least `max(1, 5*min(M,N))` elements from `offsetRWork` (never allocated here) |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | Stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for RWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobu`: Specifies options for computing all or part of the matrix U:

  -   `= 'A'`: all M columns of U are returned in array U:
  -   `= 'S'`: the first min(m,n) columns of U (the left singular vectors) are returned in the array U;
  -   `= 'O'`: the first min(m,n) columns of U (the left singular vectors) are overwritten on the array A;
  -   `= 'N'`: no columns of U (no left singular vectors) are computed.
- `jobvt`: Specifies options for computing all or part of the matrix $V^H$:

  -   `= 'A'`: all N rows of $V^H$ are returned in the array `VT`;
  -   `= 'S'`: the first min(m,n) rows of $V^H$ (the right singular vectors) are returned in the array `VT`;
  -   `= 'O'`: the first min(m,n) rows of $V^H$ (the right singular vectors) are overwritten on the array A;
  -   `= 'N'`: no rows of $V^H$ (no right singular vectors) are computed.

  `JOBVT` and `JOBU` cannot both be 'O'.
- `M`: The number of rows of the input matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the input matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, if `JOBU = 'O'`, A is overwritten with the first min(m,n)

  -   columns of U (the left singular vectors,
  -   stored columnwise);

  if `JOBVT = 'O'`, A is overwritten with the first min(m,n)

  -   rows of $V^H$ (the right singular vectors,
  -   stored rowwise);

  if $\mathrm{JOBU} \ne \text{'O'}$ and $\mathrm{JOBVT} \ne \text{'O'}$, the contents of A

  are destroyed.
- `s`: The singular values of A, sorted so that $S(i) \ge S(i+1)$.
- `U`: (`LDU`,M) if `JOBU = 'A'` or (`LDU`,min(M,N)) if `JOBU = 'S'`. If `JOBU = 'A'`, U contains the M-by-M unitary matrix U; if `JOBU = 'S'`, U contains the first min(m,n) columns of U (the left singular vectors, stored columnwise); if `JOBU = 'N'` or 'O', U is not referenced.
- `VT`: If `JOBVT = 'A'`, `VT` contains the N-by-N unitary matrix $V^H$; if `JOBVT = 'S'`, `VT` contains the first min(m,n) rows of $V^H$ (the right singular vectors, stored rowwise); if `JOBVT = 'N'` or 'O', `VT` is not referenced.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.
- `RWORK`: On exit, if $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, `RWORK(1:MIN(M,N)-1)` contains the unconverged superdiagonal elements of an upper bidiagonal matrix B whose diagonal is in S (not necessarily sorted). B satisfies $A = U \, B \, \mathrm{VT}$, so it has the same singular values as A, and singular vectors related by U and `VT`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if ZBDSQR did not converge

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "all-columns", "none", "overwrite", "economy"
- `TypeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `!( ( ( jobvt === "all-rows" \|\| jobvt === "economy" ) \|\| jobvt === "overwrite" ) \|\| jobvt === "none" ) \|\| ( jobvt === "overwrite" && jobu === "overwrite" )`)
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` if WORK or RWORK is too small

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `M === 0 || N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `> 0`: if ZBDSQR did not converge, `INFO` specifies how many superdiagonals of an intermediate bidiagonal form B did not converge to zero. See the description of `RWORK` above for details.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import zgesvd from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zgesvd';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
let A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const U = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const VT = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const s = new Float64Array( N );

// Using the standard interface (internally allocated workspaces):
let out = zgesvd( 'column-major', 'all-columns', 'all-rows', N, N, A, N, s, 1, U, N, VT, N, null, null );
console.log( out, s ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface (caller-provided workspaces; a 3-by-3 matrix needs at least 21 complex elements of WORK and 5*N elements of RWORK):
A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 64 );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 5 * N );
out = zgesvd.ndarray( 'all-columns', 'all-rows', N, N, A, 1, N, 0, s, 1, 0, U, 1, N, 0, VT, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out, s ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZGESVD`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZGESVD computes the singular value decomposition (SVD) of a complex M-by-N matrix A, optionally computing the left and/or right singular vectors. The SVD is written

$A = U \, \mathrm{SIGMA}$ \* conjugate-transpose(V)

where SIGMA is an M-by-N matrix which is zero except for its min(m,n) diagonal elements, U is an M-by-M unitary matrix, and V is an N-by-N unitary matrix. The diagonal elements of SIGMA are the singular values of A; they are real and non-negative, and are returned in descending order. The first min(m,n) columns of U and V are the left and right singular vectors of A.

Note that the routine returns $V^H$, not V.

</section>
